sections.summary: Removed the P17 file-name-hit branch from the path-like heuristic so an ordinary short word like "app" no longer pays a pause before its content search: isPathLikeQuery(query) is now just query.includes('/') (one argument, no ranked-row scan), and CONTENT_SEARCH_PATH_PAUSE_MS dropped 400 -> 250 ms. useRepositorySearch lost its countFileNameMatches memo and computes the path signal inline, which also took fileResults out of the content-search effect's dependencies — the effect used to cancel and reschedule the ripgrep call on every ranking identity change. countFileNameMatches was deleted from fileSearch.ts (its only consumer was that memo), removing one per-keystroke scan over the ranked rows. Expected path for the probe's 3-character 'app': 120 ms adaptive debounce + ~30 ms rg = ~150 ms, against 414-423 ms measured on the Wave 2 build. Completed in an earlier run of this agent; re-verified green in this one.

sections.summary: Three changes take the first Cmd+P off the keystroke's critical path. (a) CommandPaletteHost keeps a panelReady flag that is false on every open; one requestAnimationFrame flips it, so the keydown task commits only CommandPaletteShell — a focused input in a showModal() dialog that imports nothing from CommandPalette.tsx — and the real panel mounts on the following frame whatever it costs. (b) createFileSearchIndex keeps a one-slot cache keyed on the paths array identity and now exposes warmFileSearchIndex(paths), which builds through requestIdleCallback with a 1 s timeout (setTimeout fallback where rIC is absent) and returns its canceller so it doubles as an effect cleanup; the host warms on every snapshot.paths change and boot.tsx warms the cached-workspace paths right after createRoot().render(). I verified the identity actually lines up end to end — preload parses cachedWorkspace once via sendSync, initialWorkspacePaint returns cache.snapshot by reference, and App reads it through useState — so boot's index is the one the palette hits rather than a wasted duplicate build. (c) The panel paints FIRST_PAINT_ROWS = 12 rows on its mount commit and the rest after one frame; visibleResults feeds grouping, clampedIndex, activeAction, moveActive, trackPointer and every data-index, so the keyboard can never select a row that is not on screen, and only rendered rows instantiate an icon (12 instead of 34). I also added an in-app measure, horus:palette-open-to-focus, recorded from setVisibility(true) to the shell's focus in its layout effect, because the probe's palette.openMs is measured on the probe host across four awaited Input.dispatchKeyEvent round trips plus a polling Runtime.evaluate (Wave 2 recorded pollRoundTripMaxMs 44-67 ms), so a large share of the 89-103 ms baseline is CDP rather than app time and the <= 30 ms target is otherwise unjudgeable. Most of (a)-(c) was written by an earlier run of this agent that was restarted before logging it; this run verified it end to end, added the workspace-render assertion and the measure, and logged the section.

sections.deviations: 1. 'lazy-load row icons' is implemented as "only visible rows instantiate an icon" rather than a dynamic import('@pierre/icons'). The icon module already lives inside the palette chunk, which boot preloads and which is resident before Cmd+P; a dynamic import would either paint the first 12 rows iconless or reintroduce a Suspense boundary on the open path, and the 12-row staging removes the same work. 2. The dom test proves "the heavy index builder is not called during open" with the fileSearchIndexBuilds() counter rather than mock.module on createFileSearchIndex — bun cannot cleanly intercept a same-module import, and the counter is the stronger assertion because it also catches a build made through any other caller. 3. I added the horus:palette-open-to-focus user-timing measure, which the brief did not ask for; see reviewNotes.

G2 cannot be judged against <= 30 ms from `palette.openMs` as the probe computes it today. `measurePalette` takes `openedAt = Date.now()` on the probe host before four awaited `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` round trips, then reads `focused.at` from a `waitFor` poll (3 ms sleep plus a `Runtime.evaluate` round trip each); the Wave 2 samples recorded pollRoundTripMaxMs 44-67 ms. A large, unknown share of the 89-103 ms baseline is measurement overhead. The needs-owner probe edit below (reading the new `horus:palette-open-to-focus` measure) is what makes the target verifiable.
reviewNotes:
RISKY SPOTS

1. `palette.emptyRows` may race the new staging. The probe reads it one CDP round trip after the focused poll, but the panel now mounts a frame after the shell and fills from 12 to 34 rows a frame after that (~32 ms total). At Wave 2's round-trip costs it still reads 34, but if the round trip ever gets cheap it could read 0 or 12 and look like a P16 regression. Fix in scripts/perf/startup-probe.mjs (needs-owner, item 2 below).

2. `requestAnimationFrame` fires before paint, so the shell is not strictly guaranteed to reach the screen before the panel commits. What it does guarantee — and what the target measures — is that the panel's work is off the keydown task: `document.activeElement` is set inside the shell's layout effect during that task. I judged this correct for the metric; flag it if you wanted a guaranteed shell paint, which would need a double rAF and would cost a frame of row latency.

3. `warmFileSearchIndex` uses `requestIdleCallback`. happy-dom has no `requestIdleCallback` (verified), so the tests exercise the `setTimeout(build, 0)` fallback, not the production path. The rIC branch is unit-untested by construction.

DECISIONS

4. I added a user-timing measure the brief did not request: `PALETTE_OPEN_MEASURE = 'horus:palette-open-to-focus'`, exported from CommandPaletteHost.tsx, recorded from `setVisibility(true)` to the shell's `focus()`. Reason in blocker 2. It matches the existing `horus:*` convention (startupMetrics.ts:16), clears its previous entry so the user-timing buffer holds exactly one, and is ~12 lines. Revert it if you would rather not carry instrumentation in the palette; G2's behaviour does not depend on it.

5. I updated the plan's status table (G1 and G2 rows only, Edit-only exact replacement) because the plan says executors update it in place. plans/perf-instant-plan.md is not in my ownership list, so say the word if that was unwanted.

NEEDS-OWNER (scripts/perf/startup-probe.mjs — Track B / the reviewer owns scripts/**)

6. In `measurePalette`, after `palette.openMs = focused.at - openedAt`, add:
   `palette.openAppMs = await cdp.tryEval("performance.getEntriesByName('horus:palette-open-to-focus')[0]?.duration ?? null")`
   and `palette.openPollRoundTripMs = focused.maxRoundTripMs`; then add
   `paletteOpenAppMs: median(samples.map((s) => s.palette?.openAppMs))` to the summary object and `paletteOpenAppMs: samples.map((s) => s.palette?.openAppMs)` to the PERF metrics block.

7. Replace the immediate `palette.emptyRows` sample with a wait:
   `const rows = await cdp.waitFor("(() => { const n = document.querySelectorAll('.command-palette-results button').length; return n > 0 ? n : null })()", 500, 3)` then `palette.emptyRows = rows.value ?? 0`.

COULD NOT VERIFY

8. Everything numeric. No build, no app launch, no probe — per the brief. G1's ~150 ms and G2's frame budget are reasoned from the code and the Wave 2 sample file, not measured.

9. Whether the shell-to-panel swap is visually seamless on a real display. Both render `.command-palette-layer` as separate `<dialog>` elements, so the shell's dialog closes as the panel's opens. The DOM handoff and focus are covered by tests; a one-frame flicker would only show on device.

CROSS-TRACK

10. Track E's `onRevealDirectory` prop on CommandPalette and its directory-row call are untouched and still covered by 'selecting a folder also reveals it in the explorer'. My boot.tsx change is the single `warmFileSearchIndex(cachedPaint.snapshot?.paths)` line plus its comment, applied with Edit.
